subject: Ephemeral HSM swap runbook & validation window — MedSys cutover
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, ops@medsys.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ephemeral HSM swap runbook & validation window — MedSys cutover

Hi team,

Attaching the first cut of the runbook for the ephemeral HSM swap we discussed with MedSys. This covers:
- swap sequence for the on-prem HSM cluster (primary -> ephemeral replacement -> promotion)
- KEK derivation and key-wrapping steps (operator vs. control-plane roles)
- preflight firewall and NAC rules that MedSys needs to confirm
- rollback and zeroization checklist in case of operator failure

Attachments: ephemeral-hsm-swap-runbook-v0.9.pdf, preflight-firewall-checklist.csv, test-plan-ephemeral-keys.md

Notes / asks:
1) Laura — can you review the SLA/maintenance-window language (page 3) for Dedicated and Private offerings? I tried to be conservative but want your call on acceptable MTTR language.
2) Stephanie — can you sanity-check the attestation hooks (Section 4) and operator separation notes? I specifically called out that the operator bastion must never have unwrapped key material.
3) Marcus — please add any infra-level acceptance criteria (eg. NSGs, internal load balancer sticky session behavior) before we send to MedSys.
4) Ops (MedSys) — please confirm whether the host-level TPM attestation is available on the replacement nodes; if not, note in reply so we can switch to a sealed-wrapped flow.

Proposed validation window: 6/15 09:00 - 12:00 PT. If we go ahead, we plan a 30-minute warmup run and then the swap.

I want us to be explicit about what we require from customer side to avoid last-minute cutover stalls.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, ops@medsys.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral HSM swap runbook & validation window — MedSys cutover

Diego,

Thanks for the thorough draft — this is the right level of operational detail. A couple of quick edits:
- Page 2, "customer authority to rotate" needs a short paragraph describing DocuSign signoff for the swap (we shouldn't proceed on verbal).
- The SLA language can be tightened: propose replacing "MTTR within business day" with "target MTTR 4 hours for key recovery" and add a fallback escalation to the Redwood control plane.
- Add a short step to verify software stack versions on the ephemeral node (we had a drift incident last year).

Timing: 6/15 works for me but prefer starting at 08:30 PT so we have more daylight for rollback. Marcus, if you can confirm LB and healthcheck windows we can lock the time.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product (Private Cloud)
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, ops@medsys.com
Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral HSM swap runbook & validation window — MedSys cutover

Diego / team,

Read-through notes from security/ops:
- Attestation: the runbook references a "fresh TPM quote" for node X. We need an exact spec (PCR registers, nonce handling) and a short encoding of the expected measurement so MedSys can pre-provision attestation assertions.
- Key-wrapping: prefer a sealed-wrapping flow (wrap KEK with customer-managed wrapping key in HSM) when TPM attestation is not present. Explicitly call out which KEKs are ephemeral vs. customer-owned (table in Section 3).
- Operator separation: operator actors must be split into (1) network ops (bastion ) and (2) cryptographic operators. No single operator identity should be able to unseal production KEKs.
- Telemetry: ensure the runbook includes a short list of telemetry signals we expect during the swap (KV cache misses, sign/verify error rates, unexpected latencies). We'll use those for rollback gating.

Security action items:
* Add a step that records an HSM audit snapshot immediately prior to the swap (log id + truncated sig).
* Confirm that the z/zeroize command is available on the ephemeral node and add a confirmation checklist item that one operator is present but not entering key material.

I created JIRA INF-2142 and added a few checklist items. Also adding a link to the minimal attestation spec in the drive folder.

- Stephanie
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 03 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral HSM swap runbook & validation window — MedSys cutover

Diego / Redwood team,

Thanks for the runbook draft and the clear checklist. We can support a validation window on 6/15; 08:30 PT is preferable for us as Laura suggested. Two quick asks before we lock time:

1) Test plan: Can you send a short, runnable test plan we can execute in our staging cluster the week prior? We want to validate the wrapping/unwrapping sequence without touching production keys.
2) Firewall/NAC: our network team needs the minimal set of ports and IP ranges to allow for attestation and HSM API calls. I attached a short CSV of our current NAT ranges — please call out any required ephemeral egress ranges in the runbook.

We also need the DocuSign signoff in order to proceed — please send the signature request to security-approvals@medsys.com.

Best,
Katie Lang
Sr. Security Engineer, MedSys Health
